title: Wonders among the Jews and the Spirit in the prophets
source_text: Εἶτα πανταχοῦ μὲν ἢ πολλαχοῦ δυνάμεις ἐγίνοντο, ὡς καὶ αὐτὸς ἐν τοῖς ἑξῆς παρατίθεται Ἀσκληπιὸν εὐεργετοῦντα καὶ τὰ μέλλοντα προλέγοντα ὅλαις πόλεσιν ἀνακειμέναις αὐτῷ, οἷον τῇ Τρίκκῃ καὶ τῇ Ἐπιδαύρῳ καὶ τῇ Κῷ καὶ τῇ Περγάμῳ. καὶ Ἀριστέαν τὸν Προκοννήσιον καὶ Κλαζομένιόν τινα καὶ Ἀστυπαλαιέα Κλεομήδην· παρὰ δὲ μόνοις Ἰουδαίοις. φάσκουσιν ἀνακεῖσθαι τῷ τῶν ὅλων θεῷ. οὐδὲν ἦν σημεῖον ἢ τεράστιον, τὸ συνεργοῦν καὶ βεβαιοῦν αὐτῶν τὴν εἰς τὸν κτίσαντα τὰ ὅλα πίστιν μετὰ καὶ ἐλπίδος τῆς περὶ ἄλλου ζῆν μείζονος; ἀλλὰ πῶς οἷόν τε τὸ τοιοῦτον; εὐθέως γὰρ ἂν μετέστησαν ἐπὶ τὸ σέβειν τοὺς μαντευομένους καὶ θεραπεύοντας δαίμονας, καταλιπόντες τὸν μέχρι λόγου πεπιστευμένον αὐτοῖς βοηθεῖν θεὸν οὐδαμῶς δὲ παριστάντα τὴν ἑαυτοῦ ἐπιφάνειαν. εἰ δὲ μὴ γέγονε τοῦτο ἀλλὰ καὶ μυρία ὅσα ὑπέμενον, ἵνα μὴ ἐξομόσωνται τὸν ἰουδαϊσμὸν καὶ τὸν κατ᾿ αὐτὸν νόμον, καὶ ὁτὲ μὲν πεπόνθασιν ἐν τῇ Ἀσσυρίᾳ ὁτὲ δὲ ἐν τῇ Περσίδι ὁτὲ δὲ ὑπὸ Ἀντιόχου, πῶς οὐχὶ ἐξ εἰκότων κατασκευάζεται τοῖς ἀπιστοῦσι ταῖς παραδόξοις ἱστορίαις καὶ προφητείαις ὅτι οὐ πλάσματα ἦν τὰ τοιαῦτα, ἀλλά τι θεῖον πνεῦμα ὡς ἐν καθαραῖς ψυχαῖς τυγχάνον ταῖς τῶν προφητῶν, πάντα πόνον ὑπὲρ ἀρετῆς ἀνειληφότων, ἐκίνει αὐτοὺς πρὸς τὸ προφητεύειν τινὰ μὲν τοῖς καθ᾿ ἑαυτοὺς ἄλλα δὲ τοῖς ὕστερον ἐξαιρέτως δὲ περί τινος ἐπιδημήσοντος σωτῆρος τῷ γένει τῶν ἀνθρώπων;
pass_a_gloss: Then everywhere or in many places mighty works (δύναμις) came about, as he himself in what follows adduces (παρατίθεμαι) Asclepius doing good (εὐεργετέω) and foretelling (προλέγω) things to come to whole cities dedicated (ἀνάκειμαι) to him, such as Tricca and Epidaurus and Cos and Pergamum; and Aristeas of Proconnesus and a certain Clazomenian and Cleomedes of Astypalaea; but among the Jews alone, who say (φάσκω) they are dedicated to the God of the universe (τῶν ὅλων θεός), there was no sign or wonder helping (συνεργέω) and confirming (βεβαιόω) their faith (πίστις) in the one who created (κτίζω) the universe, with also the hope (ἐλπίς) about living another greater [life]? But how is such a thing possible? For they would at once have changed over (μεθίστημι) to revering (σέβω) the demons who divine (μαντεύομαι) and heal (θεραπεύω), having abandoned the God believed by them to help (βοηθέω) as far as word (μέχρι λόγου), but in no way presenting (παρίστημι) his own manifestation (ἐπιφάνεια). But if this did not happen, but they even endured countless (μυρία) things so as not to forswear (ἐξόμνυμι) Judaism (ἰουδαϊσμός) and the law according to it, and at one time suffered in Assyria, at another in Persia, at another under Antiochus, how is it not established (κατασκευάζω) from probabilities (ἐξ εἰκότων) for those disbelieving (ἀπιστέω) the extraordinary (παράδοξος) histories and prophecies that such things were not fictions (πλάσμα), but some divine spirit, being as in pure (καθαρός) souls in those of the prophets, who had taken up (ἀναλαμβάνω) every toil (πόνος) for virtue (ἀρετή), moved them to prophesy some things to those of their own time, others to those later, and especially (ἐξαιρέτως) about a certain saviour who would sojourn (ἐπιδημέω) among the race of men?
pass_b_english: Again: were mighty works done everywhere, or in many places (as Celsus himself relates further on, telling of Asclepius doing good and foretelling the future to whole cities dedicated to him, such as Tricca, Epidaurus, Cos and Pergamum, and of Aristeas of Proconnesus, a certain man of Clazomenae, and Cleomedes of Astypalaea), while among the Jews alone, who say they are dedicated to the God of the universe, there was no sign or wonder to support and confirm their faith in the Creator of the universe, together with their hope of another and greater life? How could that be? They would at once have gone over to worshipping the demons who give oracles and heal, and abandoned the God whom they believed to help them, though only in word, and who never showed his presence at all.

But if this did not happen, and they even endured countless sufferings so as not to renounce Judaism and the law that belongs to it, suffering at one time in Assyria, at another in Persia, at another under Antiochus, is it not shown from probability, to those who disbelieve the extraordinary histories and prophecies, that such things were not fictions, but that a divine Spirit, dwelling in the souls of the prophets as in pure souls, for they were men who had taken on every toil for the sake of virtue, moved them to prophesy some things to their own contemporaries, others to those who came later, and above all concerning a Saviour who would come to dwell among the human race?

choices.choice: Copy-text: staged source_3.json section 3 (Koetschau 3.3). The whole first period (Εἶτα … πίστιν μετὰ καὶ ἐλπίδος …;) is one question in the Greek and is kept as one. Celsus’s examples are taken up later in this book: Asclepius (3.24), Aristeas of Proconnesus (3.26) and the man of Clazomenae and Cleomedes (3.32–33); the man of Clazomenae is not named here and none is supplied. ‘μέχρι λόγου’ rendered ‘in word only’. The Jewish sufferings ‘in Assyria … in Persia … under Antiochus’ are historical references (the Assyrian exile, the Persian period as in Esther, and the persecution by Antiochus Epiphanes in 1–2 Maccabees), not quotations or verbal allusions, so no inline citation. ‘τι θεῖον πνεῦμα’ capitalised (‘a divine Spirit’): Origen means the Spirit of God who inspired the prophets; the indefinite ‘a’ keeps his deliberately general phrasing, offered as an argument from probability to unbelievers. ‘πάντα πόνον ὑπὲρ ἀρετῆς ἀνειληφότων’ (genitive with the prophets) is rendered as a descriptive clause on the prophets (‘for they were men who had taken on every toil’), which explains why their souls were pure without making it a strict condition. ‘μέχρι λόγου’ is taken with the helping: a God believed to help them, but only in word. ‘ἐξομόσωνται’ rendered ‘renounce’. No LXX renumbering arises.

‘the God who, as they believed, helped them in word only’ made ‘the God whom they believed to help them, though only in word’, so ‘only in word’ qualifies the help, not their belief (μέχρι λόγου … βοηθεῖν); ‘never showed his presence at all’ for οὐδαμῶς
added causal ‘since they had taken on every toil’ softened to a descriptive clause on the prophets (genitive participle ἀνειληφότων)
